answer_1.quote: Transformer-based pretrained language models (LMs) have led to a wave of advances in natural language generation tasks
datasets: Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification Challenge Dataset

answer_2.quote: We evaluate our generated outputs for toxicity, fluency and diversity. Following previous evaluation methods , we characterize generation toxicity with the toxicity score given by Perpective API , a widely-used toxicity detection tool. ... Generation fluency and diversity are measured using the mean perplexity of generated continuations and the mean number of distinct n-grams as in the previous research among n = 25 generations for each prompt.

answer_4.quote: In addition to automatic evaluation, we carry out human evaluation on toxicity and fluency of generated text to compare baselines with our method. ... each continuation is evaluated by two annotators
answer_4.guideline: who rate fluency on a scale of 1 to 5 (1 being very confused and 5 being very fluent) and rate toxicity on a scale of 0 to 2 (0 being nontoxic at all, 1 being mildly toxic and 2 being toxic). Annotators are told that toxic generation is a rude, disrespectful, or unreasonable comment that is likely to make people leave a discussion
